paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the Father's welcome is bigger than anything we can earn or lose. The younger son rehearsed a whole speech about being a hired servant, and the father never let him get to that part. He ran to him, embraced him, and kissed him (Luke 15:20). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I know what it is to feel like you're past useful. The father's love doesn't wait for you to clean up first.

Now look at the older son, because he's the one who sneaks up on you. He stayed home, served for years, and still stood outside the party angry (Luke 15:28-29). His father came out and pleaded with him too, and told him, 'Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours' (Luke 15:31). I think this one is for the baker who has been faithful a long time, because it's easy to start counting what you did and forget who you're with. Being near the father was always the prize, and it was never a paycheck.

So here's what to carry out of my bakery today. If you've wandered, get up and go home, because the father is already watching the road. If you've stayed, come inside and be glad when somebody else is found, because the father says it was fitting to celebrate (Luke 15:32). Jesus ends it with the father's words, 'he was lost and is found,' and He leaves the older son's answer open. Now the question lands on you, friend, and the door is open and the music is playing.
